summary_paragraph: A young woman with a history of tracheobronchomalacia and chronic tracheostomy was admitted for green sputum from her tracheostomy, chest and throat pain, chills, and odynophagia. She had recently completed a course of outpatient vancomycin for MRSA tracheitis. On admission, she was unable to swallow pills due to pain and required IV morphine. Evaluation showed no fever, leukocytosis, or radiographic abnormalities. Sputum culture revealed gram-positive cocci, and she was treated with intravenous vancomycin. Her symptoms improved, and she was transitioned to oral doxycycline. Blood cultures remained negative. She was discharged home on a 10-day course of doxycycline and ondansetron for nausea, with follow-up planned with infectious disease and pulmonary specialists for possible MRSA decolonization.
problems: Bronchopulmonary dysplasia originating in the perinatal period
